title: When the gate buzzes

dating.label: Neo-Assyrian · Neo/Late Babylonian witnesses
dating.note: The linked source witnesses carry Neo-Assyrian, Neo/Late Babylonian period labels. These date surviving manuscripts, not the composition.

purpose: When a man's gate makes a buzzing sound, smear a pounded paste on the door-jamb with an incantation, wash it off into a cloth, then bury a fleece with sulphur and oil at the outer gate and door socket so that sorcery cannot approach.
attribution: Omen-triggered ritual instruction; the practitioner acts

phases.name: Paste on the door-jamb
phases.idea: A paste is pounded, charged by incantation, smeared on the jamb and washed off.

phases.name: Deposit at the gate
phases.idea: A fleece with sulphur and oil is buried at the gate.

steps.title: Pound sulphur, gypsum and red paste together
steps.shortTitle: Pound sulphur, gypsum and red paste together
steps.shortDescription: Sulphur, gypsum and red paste are pounded together into a mixture.
steps.summary: Sulphur, gypsum and red paste are pounded together into a mixture.
steps.evidence: Line 2 glosses "sulphur, gypsum, red paste together pound in mixture"; line 3 begins "mix (up)".

image.alt: Illustrative reconstruction: pound sulphur, gypsum and red paste together.
image.note: Illustrative reconstruction of the documented objects and action; form, colour and staging beyond the glossed text are conjectural.

steps.title: Recite "Furious, furious … tear out the sorcery"
steps.shortTitle: Recite "Furious, furious … tear out the sorcery"
steps.shortDescription: The incantation "Furious, furious, arisen evil …" ends with a command to tear out the sorcery.
steps.summary: The incantation "Furious, furious, arisen evil …" ends with a command to tear out the sorcery.
steps.evidence: Lines 3–5 gloss the incipit "furious furious arisen bad … who? opponent … tear out sorcery". The addressee is unclear; classed as dismissal of the sorcery.

steps.title: Recite into the paste; apply it to the door-jamb
steps.shortTitle: Recite into the paste; apply it to the door-jamb
steps.shortDescription: The incantation is recited three times into the mixture, which goes on the door-jamb of the man's house gate.
steps.summary: The incantation is recited three times into the mixture, which goes on the door-jamb of the man's house gate.
steps.evidence: Line 6 glosses "incantation this thrice to interior count; (door-)jamb gate house man him". No verb of smearing is glossed; application to the jamb is inferred from line 7, where the mixture is washed off. Reuses action type anoint-door.

steps.title: Wash the paste off with silt into a cloth
steps.shortTitle: Wash the paste off with silt into a cloth
steps.shortDescription: Afterwards the mixture is washed off with silt, into a cloth trimming, and the harm is released.
steps.summary: Afterwards the mixture is washed off with silt, into a cloth trimming, and the harm is released.
steps.evidence: Lines 7–8 gloss "silt wash (off) after mixture that mix; in (a cloth trimming) wash (off), intact, released"; line 9 "(so that) sorcery not come near man and house". Whether the cloth is then disposed of is not stated.

steps.title: Wrap sulphur and oil in combed fleece
steps.shortTitle: Wrap sulphur and oil in combed fleece
steps.shortDescription: An alkaline plant, henbane(?) and a good mixture, with sulphur and oil, are enclosed in combed fleece.
steps.summary: An alkaline plant, henbane(?) and a good mixture, with sulphur and oil, are enclosed in combed fleece.
steps.evidence: Line 10 glosses "(an alkaline plant), henbane?, mixture good"; line 11 "sulphur, oil, combed, in fleece surround". Only sulphur and oil are clearly wrapped; the line-10 plants are probably part of the same deposit.

steps.title: Bury it at the outer gate and door socket
steps.shortTitle: Bury it at the outer gate and door socket
steps.shortDescription: The fleece deposit is buried at the outer gate and at the door's pivot socket, so that the sorcery is lost and cannot come near the man and his house.
steps.summary: The fleece deposit is buried at the outer gate and at the door's pivot socket, so that the sorcery is lost and cannot come near the man and his house.
steps.evidence: Line 11 ends "in gate outer and socket for doorpost door"; line 12 glosses "cover (in earth), sorcery be lost"; line 13 "to man and house not come near". Whether one or two deposits is unclear.
